question:
A transistor-based LC oscillator uses a resonant tank circuit with inductance $L=10\,\text{mH}$ and capacitance $C=0.10\,\mu\text{F}$. Assume the oscillation frequency is approximately the resonant frequency

 $f_0=\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}.$ 

(a) Calculate $f_0$.

(b) Explain how the transistor (used as an amplifier) compensates for energy losses in the LC tank to maintain oscillations.

(c) State the Barkhausen criterion and explain what happens when $|A\beta|<1$ and when $|A\beta|>1$.

(d) A student claims: “Once oscillations start, the supply is not needed because LC will keep oscillating forever.” Evaluate this claim using energy-loss reasoning.

(e) Draw a schematic block diagram of an oscillator showing: amplifier, feedback network (LC tank/feedback path), and indicate where the output is taken.

options.A: $f_0\approx 5.0\,\text{kHz}$; transistor supplies energy each cycle to compensate losses; Barkhausen: net phase $0^{\circ}$ and $|A\beta|=1$ for steady amplitude; without supply, losses damp oscillations.
options.B: $f_0\approx 50\,\text{Hz}$; transistor removes energy from tank to keep oscillations; Barkhausen: $|A\beta|=0$; without supply, oscillations increase.
options.C: $f_0\approx 0.5\,\text{MHz}$; LC oscillates forever without losses so supply is unnecessary; Barkhausen: phase condition not required.
options.D: $f_0$ cannot be computed without transistor $\beta$; oscillation frequency depends mainly on $\beta$ not on $L$ and $C$.
